small_guidance:
- Enable TF32: change `allow_tf32=False` to `allow_tf32=True` in `tl.dot`. With fp32 inputs on Ampere/Ada, TF32 nearly doubles tensor-core throughput and still passes the 5e-2 tolerance. This is likely the single biggest win.
- Expand autotune to include larger K tiles and more stages for the K=8192 loop: e.g. `BLOCK_K=128` with `num_stages=4`, plus a `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64` shape; K is huge so deeper pipelining pays off.
- Drop the per-iteration `mask_m`/`mask_n` on the K-loop loads since M=N=8192 are exact multiples of common tile sizes — switch to unmasked loads in the hot loop (keep masks only on the bias load and final store) to remove predication overhead.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a TF32 tensor-core GEMM with split-K or persistent-CTA scheduling. M=N=K=8192 is large enough that a persistent kernel with one CTA per SM iterating over output tiles can amortize launch and improve L2 reuse versus the current one-tile-per-program design.
- Pre-transpose the weight to `(K, N)` once in `__init__` so B-loads are stride-1 along N (currently B uses `weight.stride(0)` as the N-stride which is K=8192 — a strided gather). Storing the transpose contiguously will give coalesced vector loads on B in the hot loop.
- Fuse bias+multiplier+leaky_relu in the epilogue as already done, but consider also storing in fp16/bf16 if the downstream tolerance allows — however fp32 output is required here, so focus instead on cp.async-style pipelining via `num_stages>=4` over `BLOCK_K=64-128`.
